title: divergence pipeline parameters
description: A Nextflow pipeline for identifying putative paralogs and calculating their divergence

input_output_options.title: Input/output options
input_output_options.description: Define where the pipeline should find input data and save output data.

input.description: Path to comma-separated file containing the protein FASTA and matching CDS FASTA for each species.
input.help_text: Three columns: `species`, `fasta` (proteome) and `cds` (nucleotide CDS). Record IDs in `cds` must match the protein IDs in `fasta` exactly -- `bin/get_matching_cds.py` produces files in this form. Every species' CDS is needed because codon alignments are built for whole orthogroups, not only the target species.

target_species.description: Species whose paralogs are analysed. One name, a comma-separated list, or 'all'.
target_species.help_text: Each name is matched as a prefix against the OrthoFinder Orthogroups.tsv header and must match exactly one column. 'all' selects every species in the table. An orthogroup is analysed when any target species has at least --min_paralogs genes in it. Pairs are only ever formed within a species, so orthologs are never reported; ortholog distances can be read off the published dS and dN trees.

outdir.description: The output directory where the results will be saved. You have to use absolute paths to storage on Cloud infrastructure.

email.help_text: Set this parameter to your e-mail address to get a summary e-mail with details of the run sent to you when the workflow exits. If set in your user config file (`~/.nextflow/config`) then you don't need to specify this on the command line for every run.

batch_size.description: Number of orthogroups handled inside a single MAFFT or CODEML task.

analysis_options.title: Analysis options
analysis_options.description: Options controlling orthogroup selection and dS estimation.

genetic_code.description: PAML genetic code index (`icode`) used by CODEML and for codon alignment.
genetic_code.help_text: 0 is the universal code. 3 is the Mycoplasma/Spiroplasma code (NCBI table 4), where TGA encodes Trp rather than a stop. Using the wrong code here silently corrupts both the codon alignment and dS.

min_paralogs.description: Minimum number of target-species genes for an orthogroup to be analysed.

max_orthogroup_seqs.description: Skip orthogroups with more sequences than this. 0 disables the limit.
max_orthogroup_seqs.help_text: Alignment and tree-fitting cost grows steeply with orthogroup size, and gene family sizes have a long tail, so one enormous family can dominate a batch. Cap it if runtime is skewed.

max_target_paralogs.description: Skip orthogroups with more target-species genes than this. 0 disables the limit.
max_target_paralogs.help_text: Pairwise cost is quadratic in the number of target paralogs, so a 100-member family is ~4950 pairwise CODEML runs.

codeml_method.description: CODEML `method`: 0 optimises all branches simultaneously, 1 one at a time.
codeml_method.help_text: Defaults to 1, which is ~25x faster at n >= 32 for dS identical to 5 d.p. on simulated data. Only affects runmode 0 (the tree fit).

skip_pairwise.help_text: The pairwise estimate is independent of the gene tree, so disagreement with the tree-based estimate flags saturation, a bad alignment or a bad topology. Skipping it saves time but removes that signal.

codeml_timeout.description: Abandon a single CODEML or YN00 call after this many seconds. 0 waits indefinitely.
codeml_timeout.help_text: Deeply saturated sequences make the ML optimiser crawl toward an unbounded dS, so a single orthogroup can consume an entire task's time budget. A timed-out estimate is reported as NA and the rest of the orthogroup still runs. Leave at 0 unless runs are being killed by scheduler time limits.

institutional_config_options.title: Institutional config options
institutional_config_options.description: Parameters used to describe centralised config profiles. These should not be edited.
institutional_config_options.help_text: The centralised nf-core configuration profiles use a handful of pipeline parameters to describe themselves. This information is then printed to the Nextflow log when you run a pipeline. You should not need to change these values when you run a pipeline.

custom_config_version.description: Git commit id for Institutional configs.

custom_config_base.help_text: If you're running offline, Nextflow will not be able to fetch the institutional config files from the internet. If you don't need them, then this is not a problem. If you do need them, you should download the files from the repo and tell Nextflow where to find them with this parameter.

generic_options.title: Generic options
generic_options.description: Less common options for the pipeline, typically set in a config file.
generic_options.help_text:
These options are common to all nf-core pipelines and allow you to customise some of the core preferences for how the pipeline runs.

Typically these options would be set in a Nextflow config file loaded for all pipeline runs, such as `~/.nextflow/config`.

publish_dir_mode.description: Method used to save pipeline results to output directory.
publish_dir_mode.help_text: The Nextflow `publishDir` option specifies which intermediate files should be saved to the output directory. This option tells the pipeline what method should be used to move these files. See [Nextflow docs](https://www.nextflow.io/docs/latest/process.html#publishdir) for details.

email_on_fail.description: Email address for completion summary, only when pipeline fails.
email_on_fail.help_text: An email address to send a summary email to when the pipeline is completed - ONLY sent if the pipeline does not exit successfully.

plaintext_email.description: Send plain-text email instead of HTML.

monochrome_logs.description: Do not use coloured log outputs.

validate_params.description: Boolean whether to validate parameters against the schema at runtime

pipelines_testdata_base_path.description: Base URL or local path to location of pipeline test dataset files

trace_report_suffix.description: Suffix to add to the trace report filename. Default is the date and time in the format yyyy-MM-dd_HH-mm-ss.

help_full.description: Display the full detailed help message.

show_hidden.description: Display hidden parameters in the help message (only works when --help or --help_full are provided).
